exposure: advanced maternal age (>= 35 years at first pregnancy)
outcome: antepartum complications (anemia, antepartum hemorrhage, hypertensive disorders of pregnancy, diabetes mellitus, preterm labor)
intrapartum complications (poor progress of labor, cephalo-pelvic disproportion)
cohort: 78 booked primigravidae aged 35 years or more who delivered at the Federal Teaching Hospital Abakaliki from 1st January 2012 to 31st December 2016, each matched with two primigravid women aged 20-25 years who delivered during the same period.
finding: Elderly primigravidae (>= 35 years) experienced a higher incidence of antepartum and intrapartum complications, preterm delivery, and perinatal mortality compared to younger primigravidae.
mod_finding: Almost half of the elderly primigravidae group were delivered by caesarean section, the most common indication being maternal request due to prolonged infertility.
